layers.note: The tree of the south Puget Sound prairies and oak woodlands, and of dry, rocky slopes.

moisture.note: Dry ground: prairie edges, gravelly outwash and rocky slopes.

heat_load.note: Warm, sunny ground; favours slopes facing south and west.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,000 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: Holds dry slopes and bluffs as well as flats.

shade_tolerance.note: Shade intolerant: Douglas-fir overtops and kills it where fires no longer burn.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS).
